messages.subject: having trouble with reactivity
parts:
Hi folks - I've been trying to follow the tutorials, but I'm nonetheless having trouble getting reactive to be, well, reactive.  I am building an app that reads in a csv file, converts it to be R friendly, and plots the data (and eventually,d oes a host of other operations to it.)   It reads in my data fine.. but if I reload another file,, it does not load.  here is my code:
(originally I dd the 'reactive' call more directly, but I tried the quoted style to see if it made a difference; it did not):


server:

library(shiny)
library(ggplot2)

# Define server logic
shinyServer(function(input, output) {

 
  output$contents <- renderTable({
   
   inFile <- input$file1
 
   if (is.null(inFile))
     return(NULL)
 
  
  mycsv <- quote ({   
    read.csv(inFile$datapath, header=input$header, sep=input$sep, quote=input$quote)
  })
  
   mydata <- reactive(mycsv, quoted = TRUE)
  
 })

# 'split' the data, in case we have 2 groups in the dataset
 datalist <- split(mydata, mydata$group)
 
# so datalist[1] is 1 group, datalist[2] is the other, if it exists    

  output$plot <- renderPlot({
   
    p <- qplot(value, data = subset(mydata, group==mydata$group[1]), colour = "cyan")
    p + geom_histogram(binwidth = 1, fill = "white")
    print(p)   
  #  if (length(datalist > 1)) {
      q <- qplot(value, data = subset(mydata, group==mydata$group[2]), colour = "red")
      q + geom_histogram(binwidth = 1, fill = "white")
      print(q)
 #   }
   
  })
 
  # Generate a summary of the data
  output$summary <- renderPrint({
    summary(mydata$value)
  })
 

ui:

: library(shiny)


shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
 
  # Application title
  headerPanel("Assessment and Monitoring Analysis Tools"),
 
  sidebarPanel(
    tags$head(
      tags$style(type="text/css", "select { max-width: 150px; }"),
      tags$style(type="text/css", "textarea { max-width: 135px; }"),
      tags$style(type="text/css", ".jslider { max-width: 150px; }"),
      tags$style(type='text/css', ".well { max-width: 200px; }"),
      tags$style(type='text/css', ".span4 { max-width: 200px; }")
    ),
   
    fileInput('file1', 'Choose CSV File',
              accept=c('text/csv', 'text/comma-separated-values,text/plain')),
    tags$hr(),
    checkboxInput('header', 'Header', TRUE),
    radioButtons('sep', 'Separator',
                 c(Comma=',',
                   Semicolon=';',
                   Tab='\t'),
                 'Comma'),
    radioButtons('quote', 'Quote',
                 c(None='',
                   'Double Quote'='"',
                   'Single Quote'="'"),
                 'Double Quote')
  ),
     
  mainPanel(
    tabsetPanel(
      tabPanel("plot",
               verbatimTextOutput("summary"),
               plotOutput("plot"),
               p(paste("Histogram of values from csv"))),
      tabPanel("Data Table", tableOutput("contents")),
      tabPanel("Threshold Analysis"),
     
      tabPanel("2 Sample T-Test"),
     
      tabPanel("Paired T-Test"),
     
      tabPanel("ANOVA")
    )
  )
   
    )
)

I can (and have) follow the tutorial example (09) of reading a csv file, and making the table output reactive, BUT I need to also capture the csv data as an R dataset (vs a Shiny object) and be able to 'reactivate' some plots that use that same data.  how to I ..'layer' both the output table of data and the plotting of said data together in server?
